# AArch32 decoder

`uml_arm64_aarch32_decoder` is the one decoder for the 32-bit Arm line. Both
arm64 engines and the AArch32 semantic library share it. It decodes A32,
T16 and T32 words, in the IT state the caller holds, and answers with the
instruction's form, condition, length, operands and IT effect. It includes no
engine, holds no state, and is a CPU-layer `shared` target.

## Contract

`decode.hpp` is the decoder's interface and `semantics.hpp` the semantic
library's; their comments state what each call takes, returns and guarantees,
including the fault ordering and what each exit leaves in the PC and
ITSTATE, which the engines follow. `a32_profile.hpp` builds the `Profile` an
engine decodes against from the host.

The profile is Armv8-A AArch32 at EL0 (see
[`docs/architecture.md`](../../../../docs/architecture.md) and
[`docs/a32-instruction-coverage.md`](../../../../docs/a32-instruction-coverage.md)):
whatever it lacks is undefined, never guessed. The decoder implements these
choices on top of the Arm XML:

- SWP and SWPB, which Armv8 AArch32 does not have, decode as unallocated, so
  an engine raises the undefined-instruction event for them whatever the
  condition and leaves the choice to the guest kernel, which emulates them
  behind `abi.swp` ([`kernel/common/README.md`](../../../../kernel/common/README.md)).
- SETEND, SETPAN, SRS, RFE, ERET, HVC, SMC, HLT, DCPS, the banked-register and
  user-register forms of MRS, MSR, LDM and STM, and LDC and STC are undefined
  at EL0.
- MRS and MSR reach the APSR only, and VMRS and VMSR reach FPSCR only
  (including `VMRS APSR_nzcv, FPSCR`). An MSR whose x field would write
  PSTATE.E is undefined, and its c field is ignored at EL0.
- CPS is a NOP at EL0 and BXJ behaves as BX.
- An A32 data-processing instruction with S set and Rd 15 (an exception return)
  and an encoding whose should-be-zero or should-be-one bits differ are
  UNPREDICTABLE, hence undefined.
- The hint encodings of features the profile lacks (ESB, TSB, CLRBHB) are
  NOPs, as are the reserved hint encodings whose should-be bits hold; one that
  differs is UNPREDICTABLE, hence undefined.

## The table

`a32_encodings.hpp`, `a32_encodings.cpp` and `a32_operand_decode.cpp` are
generated by `tests/tooling/arm64/generate_a32_encoding_table.py` from the
pinned Arm AArch32 XML release, the profile's choices
(`tests/tooling/arm64/a32_profile_policy.py`) and LLVM MC, a tooling-time
oracle that no build uses. Never edit them.

`form_operation.hpp` groups the forms into operations (`Op`) by mnemonic. It is
the one such table: the semantic library adds its handlers and transfer modes
to it, and the JIT's compiler adds its classes for the VFP, Advanced SIMD and
Armv8 forms.

The unit test `arm64-aarch32-decoder` decodes the stored sample words of every
row and the whole 16-bit Thumb space and compares the answers against
`a32_expected.py`, an independent evaluation of the same pseudocode and rules,
and against what LLVM MC decodes (`tests/unit/arm64/aarch32_decoder/`).
[`docs/testing.md`](../../../../docs/testing.md#cpu-instruction-tests) has the
commands.

## The semantic library

`uml_arm64_aarch32_semantics` is the one C++ implementation of what the
decoder accepts, for the engines' slow paths and long tails and for the
corpus's model lane (`semantics.hpp`). It is a CPU-layer `shared` target that
includes no engine, works on `CpuState` alone and reaches guest memory only
through the caller's `A32Memory`. The engines reach it through `execute_a32`;
`step_a32`, which fetches and decodes as well, is the model lane's and the
semantic tests' entry. It covers the whole profile, A32 and T32
([`docs/a32-instruction-coverage.md`](../../../../docs/a32-instruction-coverage.md)
lists the forms).

- The unit tests that require a lowered form to stay out of the library link
  `uml_arm64_aarch32_semantics_exit_counting`, the library built with per-form
  counters of `execute_a32` calls (`semantics_exit_counters.hpp`); the library
  the products link has none.
- FPSCR is split across `CpuState` as the engines hold it: the control bits in
  `fpcr`, the cumulative flags and QC in `fpsr`, and N, Z, C and V in
  `a32_fpscr_nzcv`; Len, Stride and the trap enables read as zero and ignore
  writes.
- The profile presents BFloat16, the 8-bit matrix multiply and FHM only where
  the host has them, but the library implements all three without them, so the
  corpus model lane tests every form on any host.

## Build and test

```sh
cmake --workflow --preset check-unit
```

Focused tests: `ctest -R '^arm64-aarch32-decoder$'`. The corpus and the
semantic library's tests are in
[`docs/testing.md`](../../../../docs/testing.md#cpu-instruction-tests).
